Stops the voice-3 sound effect at once: script pointer high byte $E8 = 0 (idle), $D412 = 0 (gate and waveform off), wait counter $EA81 = 0, and $98 = 0 so the music may use voice 3 again (music_voice3_busy $9593). Called from the shop ($786D) and $863A/$8677.

Sound-effect player, once per frame from the raster IRQ ($8FBD). Idle while $E8 = 0. Counts the wait $EA81 down: at 0 it runs the script (sfx_run $3C31); when it equals $EA80 the gate is released ($D412 = $EA7D); $EA80 is only ever $FF ($3D4B), so that release never comes from here. Then the trill: while $EA7E is non-zero it is negated each frame and voice 3's frequency high byte is $EA83 + $EA7E + 1, alternating above and below; the slide: $EA84 positive raises $EA83 by 1 a frame, negative lowers it ($D40F).

Runs script commands until one that waits: fetches a byte (sfx_fetch), low nibble = command 1-15 (0 = end: $EA81, $E8 and $98 cleared), high nibble = its argument; jumps to the handler from $3D84/$3D93 through the vector $E9/$EA with the byte in A (and $EA7B). Commands 1-3 end the frame, 4 and above continue with the next byte. Handlers: 1 wait, 2 gate note, 5 sub-commands, 6 note, 7 trill, A count, B pulse width, C waveform, D bend; 3, 4, 8, 9, E, F do nothing ($3D5B).
JMP ($00E9) with A = the command byte $EA7B: calls the handler sfx_run picked.
Returns the next script byte in A: LDA ($E7,X) with X = 0, then advances the pointer $E7/$E8; X is preserved in $EA7C.
Command 1: wait. $EA81 = sfx_durations[high nibble] frames ($3D5C). Also the first half of command 2.
Sets the wait (sfx_cmd_wait) and turns the gate on: $D412 = $EA7D OR 1.
Command 2: wait by the high nibble, gate on, then falls into command 6 (sfx_cmd_note) with the next byte as the note.
Command 6: the next script byte is a note number (0-95, C0-B7): voice 3 frequency from $3E5A (low) and $3DFA (high), the high byte also kept in $EA83 for trills and slides; the note in $EA86.
Command 5: a sub-command chosen by the high nibble AND 7 through $3DA2/$3DAA and $E9/$EA: 0 ADSR ($3CB8), 1 slide ($3CC5), 2 loop ($3CCC), 3-7 nothing.
Sub-command 0: the next two script bytes go to voice 3's attack/decay ($D413) and sustain/release ($D414).
Sub-command 1: the whole command byte goes to $EA84, the slide: $15 (bit 7 clear) raises the pitch each frame, $95 lowers it (sfx_tick).

Sub-command 2: the next byte is a negative offset; $EA7F is counted down and, until it reaches 0, the script pointer moves back by the offset (plus the $FF carry), repeating the commands before it. $EA7F comes from command A.
Command 7: $EA7E = high nibble, the trill width in frequency high-byte steps (0 = off).
Command A: $EA7F = high nibble, the repeat count for the loop sub-command.
Command B: pulse width of voice 3, high nibble to $D411, the next byte to $D410.
Command C: control register of voice 3 = sfx_waveforms[high nibble] ($3D74) to $D412; $EA7D = the same with the gate bit clear.
Command D: adds the high nibble, sign-extended from the command byte's bit 7, to the frequency high byte $EA83 and $D40F.

Starts sound effect Y (0-4) on voice 3 unless one is playing ($E8 non-zero): wait 1, ADSR, pulse, frequency and control of voice 3 cleared, $EA7D/$EA7E/$EA84 = 0, $98 = $EA80 = $FF (voice 3 taken from the music), pointer $E7/$E8 from $3DB4/$3DB9. Cold start, the game's first instruction; RUN/STOP+RESTORE also lands here (nmi_restore_handler). SEI, stack $FF, screen blanked, CIAs quietened ($8FD8); NMI vector $FFFA = $6425, IRQ vector $FFFE = $8E76; $01 = $35 (RAM at $A000/$E000, I/O in), $00 = $2F; the 47 VIC registers $D000-$D02E from the table at $371D; VIC bank 1 ($DD00 bits 0-1 = %10); zero page $02-$FE cleared; $4000-$5FFF cleared. Builds two 256-byte lookup tables: $E700 = the byte with its four 2-bit multicolour pixels in reverse order (a horizontal mirror), $E600 = each pixel pair with either bit set turned into %11 (x OR its bit-pairs swapped). Copies the character ROM's upper-case set, $D008-$D3FF, to $5808 (char 0 left alone) with CHAREN off, then 128 bytes from $36A4 over chars $1B-$2A (the ACTIVISION logo glyphs, and '(' drawn as '!'), and the letter O's shape over the digit 0 ($5878 -> $5980). Colour RAM cleared to 0, row 24 set to white; the 120-byte line buffer $EB00-$EB77 filled with spaces, $EB78 = $FF. Then falls into rle_unpack.

Run-length unpacker: rebuilds the video bank from the packed stream at $B408 (pointer $0B/$0C) into $4000 onwards (pointer $23/$24). A byte other than $11 is copied; $11 is followed by a count and stands for that many zero bytes (a count of 0 means 256). Stops when the source pointer reaches $BFF8 or beyond (the test is only low byte >= $F8 with high byte >= $BF). Continues at build_mirrored_sprites.
rle_unpack's helper: advance the packed-stream pointer $0B/$0C by one byte.
rle_unpack's helper: advance the output pointer $23/$24 by one byte.

Makes left-facing copies of eight sprite shapes after unpacking: the four shapes at $4640-$473F go to $4F00-$4FFF and the four at $4740-$483F to $5000-$50FF, each 3-byte row written with its bytes in reverse order and every byte passed through the mirror table $E700, so each copy is the multicolour shape flipped left to right. Steps X down by 3 from $FC, skipping the 64th (padding) byte of each shape; stops when X passes zero. (Both areas are in the rebuilt video bank.)

Sprite 1 multicolour, sprite 0 pointer $0D ($4340), both at X $40 Y $80. Lyric pointer $21/$22 = $6443 (lyric_text), music reset ($93E2, $88-$8A = $FF, $929C). Measures the last raster line: $EA73 = $FF if its low byte is $14 or more (PAL, 312 lines) and $00 otherwise (NTSC). Raster IRQ at line $B8, screen on (D011 $18, D016 $1B multicolour), background colours 1 white and 2 red; speaks phrases 1 and 3 ($8DB9), then zeroes the tick $08 and the lyric index $97, resets the music again and enables interrupts.

The title screen's main loop, once per frame: waits for raster line $28 on the top half, then puts D011 ($18), D016 ($1B) and the background colours back after the IRQ's lower split, and jumps over the name_entered_flag byte to title_frame_work.

Flag, a byte kept in the code: 0 in the image, set to 1 at $74CA once a name has been typed and copied to $EAB3; read at $7485. With F3 at the title and this flag set, the interview is skipped: the stored name and account are decoded again ($9155) and play goes straight to vehicle selection (seen in the simulator). With the flag clear F3 runs the full interview like F1. Neither the cold start nor RESTORE clears it, so it lasts until the machine is reset.

Title loop body: reads the joystick ($96CA) and keyboard ($96E8), plays the tune ($93F0), $91C8, and ticks the lyric timer (lyric_timer_tick); on PAL ($EA73 set) one frame in eight does $91C8 and the tick twice, 9 ticks per 8 frames, about 56 a second against 60 on an NTSC machine, so the song keeps nearly the same tempo. Scrolls the lyric window while $9A counts down: when $9A&7 reaches 7 rows 21-22 ($5748) move up to rows 20-21 and row 22 is cleared, when $9A&15 reaches 0 the next lyric line is printed on row 22 ($9682). SPACE ($17 = $20) when no scroll is running speaks phrase 1 ($8DB9 with A = 1). F1 or F3 (key code $19 = $20 or $28) stores the key in $EAB2, silences the SID and jumps to start_game; anything else loops to title_loop.
Writes zero to all 32 SID registers $D400-$D41F (volume off, all voices silent). Called from the title setup, on leaving the title, and at $8DB1.

Advances the title's tick counter $08 and cues the lyrics: while the lyric index $97 is below $70, when $08 equals lyric_line_times[$97] the index moves on, and if that entry is not zero $9A gets $10 added, starting a 16-step scroll that ends with the next line printed. A zero entry matches when $08 wraps to 0, so it only waits out one lap of 256 ticks. Called once a frame from title_frame_work (twice in one frame of eight on PAL) and from $8E21 while speech plays.

A silent copy of the tune sequencer's note stepping ($93F0): for each of the three voices (X = 2..0) it counts down the duration $88,x, and when it runs out reads the next note event through the voice's track list ($A2B7/$A2BA, index $82,x) and pattern ($A75B/$A75C table, offset $85,x): the event's low five bits are the next duration, it is one byte long plus one for each of bits 7 and 6, and with bit 7 set the low nibble of the byte two on goes to $94,x; an $FF after it ends the pattern (offset 0, next track entry). It writes no SID register and, unlike $93F0, does not test for a stopped voice or the track list's $FF. Called only from $8E1E, when $08&3 is 0 while digitised speech plays on the title, so the tune keeps its place and resumes in step with the lyrics.

NMI handler (vector $FFFA set at cold_start): if the key code $19 is $3F (RUN/STOP held) it blanks the screen, clears $EAB2 and restarts at cold_start (RUN/STOP + RESTORE); otherwise it returns at once. The speech player points the NMI at $F0C3 while it runs and $8E2F puts $6425 back.

Eight raster lines ($EE $EF $EF $EF $EB $EC $ED $EE), indexed by $9A&7, the lyric window's fine-scroll step. The IRQ ($8EB7-$8ECB) waits for the chosen line and writes D011 = $1B, ending the scrolled band that began at raster $C1 (where D011 = $18 OR $9A) so that the bottom rows (the copyright and Activision lines) stay still.

Lyrics of the theme song for the bouncing-ball sing-along, PETSCII, one line per $0D, 53 lines counting the first, which is a single space; $FF at $68EF ends it and the printer ($9682) goes back to $6443. Letters print as screen codes (minus $40); '(' prints as '!' because the title charset replaces char $28 (the 'GHOSTBUSTERS(' and 'I AIN'T 'FRAID OF NO GHOST(' lines). Each line is printed on row 22 of the title screen and scrolled up; the pointer is $21/$22. This part runs from 'IF THERE'S SOMETHING STRANGE' to the line before the first 'YEAH!'.
Second half of lyric_text (which starts at $6443): from 'YEAH!  YEAH!  YEAH!  YEAH!' through the closing 'WHO YOU GONNA CALL? / GHOSTBUSTERS!' refrains, up to the $FF end mark at $68EF.

112 cue times for the lyric lines, read by lyric_timer_tick with index $97 ($00-$6F): the value of the tick counter $08 at which the next line scrolls in. 53 non-zero entries, one per lyric line; each $00 entry is a wait of one full lap of $08 (256 ticks) between cues.

Title character set, multicolour, 8 bytes a character, copied by draw_title_screen to $5A00 as characters $40-$FF; this part, $6960-$6B4F, is chars $40-$7D, the letters of the GHOSTBUSTERS logo (placed by logo_map_row0-2). Pixel pairs: %01 white (D022), %10 red (D023), %11 the colour RAM's colour ($0A, red, on the logo rows 2-4; $09, white, elsewhere).

Title character set continued (starts at $6960): chars $7E-$E9, $6B50-$6EAF, the no-ghost sign (the ghost in white inside the red circle and bar), placed by no_ghost_sign_map; char $7E is the blank background inside the sign's box.

GHOSTBUSTERS logo screen map, first row: 30 character codes copied to screen $5455 (row 2, column 5) by draw_title_screen. The same page copy also puts $6EB0-$6F5F into the charset as chars $EA-$FF, which the title never shows.
GHOSTBUSTERS logo screen map, second row: 30 character codes for screen $547D (row 3, column 5).
GHOSTBUSTERS logo screen map, third row: 30 character codes for screen $54A5 (row 4, column 5).
No-ghost sign screen map: 12 rows of 18 character codes ($7E-$E9), copied by draw_title_screen to screen $54FB onwards (rows 6-17, columns 11-28), 40 bytes apart on screen.
Leaves the title for the game: sets the mode $20 to 1 (0 on the title), D011 = $1B, clears screen and colour RAM ($95B9), then falls into game_frame_loop.

Top of the game's per-frame loop, jumped back to from $8D8D: waits for the frame flag $E2 (set to 1 by the IRQ at $8FB8) and clears it, turns the screen on, or blanks it while $45 bit 7 is set ($45 is counted up at $70AE and set to $80 on reaching 4, and cleared by joystick input at $96E3), clears D011's raster bit 8, sets the border black (Y is 0 on both paths), then continues at $7000 with the per-frame work.

Per-frame work, part 1 (loop top at $6FEC): stores the $D011 and border values chosen above, counts the delay timer $7C down to 0 (set by the states that pause, e.g. $7538 after INVALID ACCOUNT NUMBER), and applies the steering request $64 of the driving scene one step per frame: negative calls $34F9 (dec $63, road shifted one character every 4 steps) and counts up to 0, positive calls $356F (inc $63) and counts down.

Only in state $15 (driving): sets $D016's fine X scroll to ($63 AND 3)*2 from the car's lateral position $63, puts the x of sprites 2 and 3 ($A4, $A6) at $63+$1E and their y ($A5, $A7) from $A992 indexed by the car bought ($5C: 0 compact, 1 hearse, 2 wagon, 3 high-performance).

While $65 is non-zero (counted by the driving code at $810B), cycles sprite 2's colour $D029 through $A996 (blue, light blue, cyan, white) in a triangle wave: ($65 AND $1F) folded to 0-15, divided by 4.

Reads the joystick ($96CA, into $33) and forces $33 and $34 to $1F (nothing pressed) unless $02 is exactly $80; then scans the keyboard ($96E8). On the first frame after the title ($20 = 1) it sets $20 = 2 and $02 = $80, zeroes $03-$05 and runs the game initialiser $9004 with X = $11 (the start-of-game variables from $9051 into $33-$44, $45-$DB zeroed, state $3A = 0), then returns to the loop top.

Every 256 frames ($08 = 0): with $02 bit 7 set (always, once the game has started) counts the idle timer $46/$45 up; when $45 reaches 4 (about 262,000 frames, some 87 minutes at 50 Hz, with no input: $96E3 and $974A clear it) it becomes $80 and $6FFB blanks the screen. The other branch ($7094-$70A7: $02 bit 7 clear, count $03 to 8, then $02 = $C0 and re-initialise with X = $0B) has no way in: $02 is $80 from the first frame on and $FF at the end ($8D24), and it never ran in the simulator.

RUN/STOP pause, in states below $2A: when the key code $19 is $3F (RUN/STOP) in states $12 and above (play), toggles $47 bit 7 (paused) once per press (bit 6 is the key-held latch) and silences the SID ($D418 = 0); otherwise clears the latch and, if not paused, restores the volume from $EA82. Seen live: PK energy stops rising while paused and resumes after a second press.

While paused ($47 bit 7) nothing below runs. Otherwise counts the frame counter $09 and, when $14 is non-zero, counts it down and re-initialises the game at 0 ($70A2). No instruction writes $14 by name, the indexed writers found do not reach it, and it stayed 0 in every simulator run: a dormant restart timer.

States $12 (map) and $24 only: recolours five of the twenty buildings per frame (index ($09 AND 3)+16, then down by 4), all twenty in four frames. The colour RAM address is $3EBA/$3ECE (lo/hi OR $D8); buildings 0-3 and 16-19 are 5x2 cells, 4-15 5x4. The colour is $3EE2[state AND 3] (multicolour: 0 green, 1 purple, 2 white, 3 red) from the building's state byte $C8+x; red alternates with green every 16 frames (the flashing haunted building). Finally paints the ZUUL and GHQ labels white ($D9CC-$D9CF, $DB2E-$DB30).

SPACE in play (states $12-$29, key $17 = $20, no report showing, $4C = 0): builds the status report in the ticker buffer $E900: the text at $3FB9 (BACKPACK POWER AT XX% OF MAXIMUM... X EMPTY TRAPS... X MEN LEFT...) in screen codes, then patches in backpack power $3E (two BCD digits, leading zero blanked by $9832), empty traps $6B and men left $3D (one digit each). $4C = 1 stops a second report until the first has scrolled off. Seen live on the map.

The bottom-line ticker, in states $12 and above while a message is in $E900 ($4B non-zero): decrements $49 by 2 each frame (the IRQ reads it at $8EF6, apparently for the fine scroll) and steps the text one character every 4 frames ($4B = window end); at 120 characters shifts the buffer down by 40. Copies 40 characters ending at $4B to row 24 ($5770), blanks past the $FF end, and clears $4A/$4B/$4C when the end has scrolled off. The 'AND #$00' at $7202 makes a frame-rate test that is always true.

States $12-$29 when no ticker message is showing: row 24 shows CITY'S PK ENERGY: (text $3A04) with the PK energy $5B/$5A as four digits at $5783-$5786 (leading zero blanked) and the balance ($9D24 formats $57-$59 as $nnnnnn into $EA14) at $578E. The second test of state < $2A at $72A6 can never fail.

Sets the PK rate mask $3C from $9DBA by the thousands digit of the PK energy ($3F below 1000, $1F, $0F, $07, $03, then $01), then types the current message ($4D non-zero, text at ($4E), set up by $9BEE): one character each frame whose $08 AND $15 is 0 ($15 = 0 prints up to 40 at once), $FF ends it. With $15 >= 3 each printable character sounds a click on SID voice 3 (pulse, $3412). $48 = $EA76 is the text colour. Returns to the loop top while typing, so the state handler waits for the message.

Typed-line input, active while $50 is non-zero ($9C83 sets it to 1): each key in $17 clicks voice 3; RETURN stores a 0 terminator at $E9FF+$50 and ends input ($50 = 0); DEL ($7F) backs up one character unless at the first; any other key is printed in white and stored at $E9FF+$50 ($9C88) while the cursor column $38 is below $25. The buffer is $EA00 on; nothing limits the length except the column. Returns to the loop top while input is open.

In the shop ($5E non-zero): draws --CREDIT-- (screen codes at $AAD3) at the top right ($541A), a row of dashes under it ($546A), and prints the balance ($9D24, message $80 = the $EA14 buffer) at row 1 column 28, every frame.

States $12 and above, every 256 frames ($09 = 0): ages each building's state $C8+x (high nibble a timer, bits 2-3 the kind, bits 0-1 the colour). A timer that wraps moves the building on via $A9B4 by kind: kind 0 to $14 (kind 1), kind 1 to $1C (kind 3), kind 2 to $F8, kind 3 to $1F (haunted, red); each stage lasts 15 ticks (3,840 frames). One already at $FF (haunted, unanswered) is cleared and adds 300 to the PK energy ($9895 with 3): the escaped Slimer. Tested in the simulator: $FF poked into a building gave +300. Live (work/verify/t4-escape.js): a building set to $10 reached $14 after 3839 frames, $1C after 7679, $1F (red) after 11519 and escaped (+300 PK, state 0) after 15359.

Unless the game is in the Zuul phase ($81), adds 1 to the PK energy ($5A, BCD, carried into $5B by $9897) every 64 frames below 1000, every 32 in the 1000s, every 16 from 2000 on (mask $3C OR $0F against $09). Seen live: 7 to 11 in 300 frames at the start.

Unless in the Zuul phase: when no building is in the first stage (a non-zero state with low nibble below 4), starts 1, 2 or 3 new ones (more as the PK thousands digit rises, counted from $3C): each is the ($23 = random $06, rotated per pick)-th free building, skipping GHQ (index $11), Zuul ($0A) and entries of $EA28 that are 0, and gets state $10.
Runs the handler for the game state $3A: JMP through the word table at $381A (state*2). Handlers end at $8D86 (next state) or $8D8D (stay), both back to the loop top.

State $00. If the game was started with F3 ($EAB2 = $28) and a name has been typed in an earlier game ($6328 = 1), decodes the stored account number ($9155; a zero result becomes $10000) and skips the interview to state 6. Otherwise prints message 1 (the franchise form, STATE YOUR NAME- LAST,FIRST:) slowly ($15 = 3), clears the input buffer $EA00-$EA13 and opens line input. Tested in the simulator: F3 on a first game gives the interview; with $6328 poked to 1 it goes to vehicle selection with $10000.

State $01: copies the typed name (20 bytes of $EA00) to $EAB3, sets $6328 = 1 (a name exists, for F3 next time; the byte lives in the code area and survives RUN/STOP-RESTORE), prints message 2 DO YOU HAVE AN ACCOUNT? and opens input.

State $02: the first typed character. Y: message 4 WHAT IS YOUR ACCOUNT NUMBER?, input, state 3. N: balance $57 = $01 ($10000 in BCD), message 3 (the bank advances $10000), state 6. Anything else: state 4's code at $7548.

State $03: converts the typed digits ($9CFC, into $23-$26) and keeps them at $EAC7-$EACA, decodes them ($9155, the routine the ready64 article names as decode-and-check) into the balance $57-$59. A zero balance means invalid: message 5 INVALID ACCOUNT NUMBER. at row $0F, delay $7C = $BF frames, state 4; otherwise state 6.

State $04: waits for the delay $7C to run out, then (also entered at $7548 from a bad Y/N answer) prints message $0C (the text at $EB00, a page of spaces at run time) from row $0D, instantly ($15 = 0), erasing the answer, and goes to state 5.
State $05: cursor to row $0C, slow typing, and back to asking DO YOU HAVE AN ACCOUNT? (sets state 1 and joins state 1 after its name copy, at $74CD, which moves on to state 2).
State $06: clears the screen ($95B9), cursor to row 1 column 1, next state. Every return to the vehicle page (a key other than 1-4 or SPACE, or a car the balance cannot pay for) starts here.
State $07: prints message 6, GHOSTBUSTING VEHICLE SELECTION: and the four cars with prices, at once ($15 = 0).
State $08: prints message 7 (YOU HAVE) slowly and saves the balance $57-$59 as the starting balance $51-$53, which the end of the game compares against ($7C43).
State $09: formats the balance ($9D24) into $EA14, strips leading spaces ($9063) and prints it (message $80, white).
State $0A: prints message 8 (PRESS SPACE BAR TO VIEW CAR OPTIONS ... GO AHEAD:), sets the car shown by SPACE ($5C) to 0 and opens input. The three bytes at $75BF are state $0B's jump back to state 6.

State $0B's SPACE branch: draws car $5C's picture ($7667 builds its characters, $95B9 clears the screen, $35E6 places them), writes the two instruction lines from $AD5C and $AD82 on rows 21-22 in black, sets multicolours ($D022 white, $D023 from $A89D by car), prints the car's description (message $B3A5[$5C] = $14-$17: cargo and top speed) and cycles $5C to the next car; each SPACE shows the next of the four.
Converts the PETSCII character in A to a screen code: space ($20) becomes 0, $40 and above lose $40, the rest pass. Used for the ticker line and the vehicle page's instructions.

State $0B: the typed line's first character. Below '1': SPACE shows the next car ($75C2), anything else back to state 6. '1'-'4': car $5C = 0-3, price from $A1D4 (hundreds/thousands BCD) and $A1D8 (ten-thousands); if the balance covers it ($9654) it is paid ($9636, BCD subtract: POKE 38454,96 makes it an RTS, so nothing is ever paid for), screen cleared, next state. Too dear, or '5' and above: back to state 6.
State $0C: builds the bought car's character set ($7667) and moves on.

Builds the car picture for car $5C in character memory: copies 768 bytes from $AAFF/$AB03 (pages $0200, $0500, $0800, $0B00 for the four cars) to $5A00-$5CFF, then the same 768 bytes again in reverse 128-byte blocks through the table at $E700 (built at run time; it reverses the order of the four 2-bit pixels in a byte) to $5D00-$5FFF: the picture is 12 columns of 16 characters, of which the image holds 6 and the other 6 are their mirror image. Seen in the simulator: the shop shows a full, symmetrical car.
State $0D: places the car picture's characters on the screen ($35E6: twelve columns from $54B2, colour 8) and moves on.

State $0E: sets up shop page $5D (0 monitoring, 1 capture, 2 storage): multicolours, message 9+$5D (the page text), instant typing; fills the five shelves $2E-$32 from $AAB3 (8 bytes a page; item codes $33-$3A), leaving empty any item whose bit in $6D ($A9A8) shows it was bought; forklift and shelf sprite positions from $AAA6 and $A988; multicolour sprites; $5E = 1 (the credit display).

State $0F, the shop each frame: eases every sprite toward its target by up to 3 pixels ($9C23), widens sprites 1-2, and places the forklift and the carried item from its position $5F (bits 2-4 the shelf row, bits 0-1 0 at the shelves and 1 at the car), the item carried $60 (shelf row + 3, 0 for none) and its car slot $61; a trap's slot moves up by 3 per trap bought ($6A). With nothing carried the column bits are cleared every frame ($775D), so the forklift only reaches the car with an item. The shelf items are sprites 3-7, their frame numbers the item codes $33-$3A.
Fire pressed at the shelves: with nothing carried, picks up the item on the forklift's shelf ($60 = row+3, car slot $61 from $AA8E by page); carrying the item from this same shelf, puts it back.

While any sprite is still moving ($9C15) starts sound effect 2 on voice 3 ($3D24) and ignores the stick; otherwise silences voice 3 ($3BDC) and reads it: right moves to the car (kept only while carrying), left back to the shelves, and at the shelves with nothing carried down/up change shelf row, capped by $AAB0 per page (3, 3, 1 items).

Fire at the car: when the car already holds its capacity ($62 >= $AA9A[$5C]: 5, 9, 11, 7) shows YOUR CAR IS LOADED TO CAPACITY. ($99CC, 7). Otherwise, carrying an item and at rest, buys it if the balance covers the price $A1DC[item-$33] (hundreds, BCD: $400, $800, $800, $400, $600, $600, $500, $8000): pays ($9636), sets its bit in $6D, counts the load $62; a trap ($38) adds to traps owned $6A and empty traps $6B, bait ($36) adds 5 dollops to $69. Item $37 has a price ($600) but is on no shelf.

Paints the bought item into the car picture: takes the carried sprite's shape (pointer $57F8+$60, data at $4000+ptr*64), shifts it right by (x-$57) AND 3 pixel pairs into $E800, and ORs it through the mask table $E600 into the car's character data at $5A00+ (address from the sprite's position); then parks the sprite off screen at its shelf and empties the shelf unless the item is a trap, which can be bought again.

Shop keys: E ends shopping, but only once a trap has been bought ($6A, TRAPS -REQUIRED-), to the next state; 1-3 switch to another page: sets state $0D and increments it at once, so page set-up $0E runs without redrawing the car, after clearing $4D, $5E and the forklift variables; other keys are ignored.

State $10, leaving the shop for the map: sprite positions $EA46-$EA55 from $37B3 and targets $EA56-$EA65 from $37C3 (sprites 4-7, the Roamers, aimed at Zuul, $62/$7A), sprite frames $C0-$C7 from $3793; copies the car picture $5A00-$5FFF to $E000-$E5FF ($9D96, 6 pages) for later, clears the music player's voice state $82-$8A ($93E2), clears the screen.

State $11: draws the city map: copies the map character set from $2A50-$304F to $5A00-$5FFF ($9D96), colour RAM to $0D (multicolour green), multicolours yellow and black; draws the thirty map pieces ($95EB with X = 29-0 and Y = 3-0; screen addresses $A861/$A87F, shapes by $EA28), a row of character $A9 in blue on row 21, the street signs (4 rows of 11 characters from $3767) and the avenue signs (row 0 from $3F06), the ZUUL ($389A, row 11) and GHQ ($B3AA, row 20) labels in white; copies the map sprites' frames, positions and targets from $C0, $EA46, $EA4E, $EA56, $37CB into $2B, $A0, $A8, $B0, $B8.

State $12, the city map each frame, part 1: saves the Roamers' positions (sprites 4-7) to $EA46; a Roamer that reaches its target $EA56 (Zuul) adds 100 PK ($9895 with 1) and is restarted ($9851). Faces each Roamer left or right (frame 8 or 9) by its target. From PK 5000 ($5B >= $50) the Keymaster and Gatekeeper (sprites 2, 3) are sent to Zuul ($3802) when they pass the point $37FE, and from 9500 wherever they are. Live: a Roamer placed next to Zuul added 100 (work/verify/t3-roamer-zuul.js); from 5000 the two met at Zuul at PK 8495-9999 in eight runs, from 9500 within 188 frames (work/verify/t6b-keymaster-spread.js, t6-keymaster.js).

When sprites 2 and 3 both stand on Zuul ($3802-$3805), once ($81 = 0): a balance below the starting one ($51-$53) goes to state $2D (the foreclosure ending); otherwise $81 = 1, the Zuul phase: GO TO ZUUL! SNEAK PAST THE MARSHMALLOW MAN... ($99CC, 9), $7C = $FF, sprites 0-1 (the logo) are sent to $63/$92 by themselves. On that frame every building state is zeroed, on each later one set to 1, and Zuul's ($D2) to $0F (red, flashing). An equal balance counts as enough: only a smaller one forecloses.
Moves the map sprites 2 pixels toward their targets ($9C25) on frames where $09 AND $3C is 0 (faster as PK rises): sprites 2-7 when active ($C0+n); sprites 0-1, the logo, only in the Zuul phase.

Outside the Zuul phase, the logo (sprite 0 at $A0/$A1) follows the joystick along the streets only: on one of the five avenues ($37D3 pairs, x) up/down move it between y $43 and $BA and snap x onto the avenue; on one of the four streets ($37DF pairs, y; a fifth pair is $FF, never matched) left/right move it between x $1E and $8D and snap y onto the street.

Sprite 1 follows the logo. For each building whose rectangle ($37D3 columns, $37DD rows; they overlap, so on a street both the building above and the one below qualify, and the lower index wins) holds the logo: $6E = that building; its colour bits show its kind if the matching instrument is owned ($A9B0 in $6D: the PK energy detector for kinds 1 and 3, the marshmallow sensor for kind 2), else 0; a haunted one ($xF) stays red, and a kind-3 building with the detector owned turns haunted ($1F) at once. Buildings not under the logo lose colours 1 and 2 (a low nibble of $0C or more is kept): by this code the pink and white warnings show only on the building the logo is at. Live (work/verify/t2-warnings.js): building 15 at $34 turned $35 (purple) with the detector and the logo beside it, stayed $34 without the detector or with only the sensor, and went back to $34 when the logo left; a Marshmallow building $C8 turned $CA (white) only with the sensor; building 8 at $3C became $1F with the detector.

A Roamer (sprites 4-7) within about 8 pixels across and 13-17 down of the logo stops where it is and, if not already marked, records the route length $66 (at least 1) in $6F-$72, the distance at which it is met on the drive (live: poking $6F put a Roamer on the road, work/verify/t13-vacuum.js). For sprites 2-3 the branch is three NOPs: an action removed.

The Keymaster and Gatekeeper (sprites 2, 3) at a street crossing ($37EA five x, $37F1 four y) pick the next crossing north, east, south or west from two bits of the random byte $06 ($37F6/$37F7 steps into $37E9/$37F0): they wander the grid.

In the Zuul phase, once the logo reaches Zuul ($63/$92) and $7C has run out: building $0A, state $16 (the drive). Otherwise fire picks the building under the logo ($6E; stick held down means the one below the street, +4). GHQ ($11) always goes; Zuul only in the Zuul phase; any other building needs empty traps ($6B, else NO EMPTY TRAPS), two men ($3D, else BACKUP MEN ARE ALL OUT OF ACTION) and backpack power ($3E, else BACKPACKS DISCHARGED); none of this tests whether the building is haunted. No route drawn ($66 = 0): state $16, else state $13.

When the marshmallow building $80 (chosen by $98D6 as PK crosses a thousand from 5000) has aged to $F8-$FB: clears it, sends the Roamers (sprites 4-7) to four points around it ($37EA/$37F1 by its column and row), clears the bait flag $68, shows -MARSHMALLOW ALERT- ($99CC, 4) and goes to state $24. The pick sets the building to $C8, so the alert comes 769-1024 frames after it. Because $68 is cleared here, bait put down before the alert is wasted; B during state $24 counts (live, work/verify/t7-marshmallow.js). A building replaced in $80 by a newer pick before its alert stays $F8 for good (stage 2 ages into $F8 again, $A9B4), live: work/verify/t17-mm-orphan.js.

Draws the route: the screen cell under the logo ($547C + row table $A915/$A92F, column (x-$1D)/4), if empty, gets the dot character $40 in colour 0 (black); each new cell counts the route length $66 up (stops at 255). $1F remembers the last cell.

Seen live: the zigzag streams from both men while fire is held. The two runs of three NOPs at $90D1 and $90DB (inside a TYA/PHA, LDY #4 ... PLA/TAY frame) look like a removed call.

Account number from the balance, run once at the end of a winning game ($8CC6): $25 = $57 and $27 = $58 (the balance in hundreds, BCD; the tens and units in $59 are dropped), $23 = the name's byte sum (account_name_sum $91B6). Check byte: ($25 + $27) mod 256, 1 if that is 0, stepped name-sum times through account_lfsr_step ($91A6; a sum of 0 steps 256 times), into $26. The 24-bit number N = $25:$26:$27 is then shifted out low bit first into the 32-bit $EAC7-$EACA ($EAC7 lowest), a 0 bit inserted after every third bit, so each nibble holds one octal digit 0-7 of N. The caller prints $EAC7, $EAC8, $EAC9, $EACA as two digits each ($9D4D), so the eight digits the player sees are N's octal digits in pairs, lowest pair first: o1 o0 o3 o2 o5 o4 o7 o6. Worked through in Python (work/agent6/acct.py): SPENGLER with $123,400 gives 64105104, VENKMAN,PETER with the same balance 64405104.

Checks an account number against the name and yields the balance (called at $748E for F3's replay and at $7520 after the number is typed): reads the eight nibbles of $EAC7-$EACA most significant first ($EACA high nibble, low nibble, then $EAC9 ... $EAC7), keeps the low three bits of each (bit 3 is shifted out unchecked, so a typed 8 reads as 0 and 9 as 1) into the 24-bit $25 (high), $26, $27; recomputes the check byte from $25 + $27 and the name sum exactly as account_encode ($90EE) does; if it differs from $26, $25 and $27 are zeroed. Leaves $57 = $25 and $58 = $27 (the balance in hundreds); $59 is not touched. A zero result is what the caller treats as INVALID ACCOUNT NUMBER. Tested in the simulator by typing: VENKMAN,PETER with 64405104 gives $123400, with 64485184 also $123400, with 64405105 the number is refused. Nothing checks that $25 and $27 are valid BCD: ANDY with 777 gives $57 = $FC and the vehicle page shows YOU HAVE $?<0000.

One step of the account check byte's 8-bit shift register at $07 (ASL/EOR/ASL/EOR/ASL/ASL/EOR, then ASL and ROL $07): $07 moves left one bit and the new bit 0 is bit 3 XOR bit 4 XOR bit 5 XOR bit 7 of the old value, a maximal-length register (x^8 + x^6 + x^5 + x^4 + 1). From any non-zero value it repeats after 255 steps (checked in Python over all 256 values), so the 256 steps a name sum of 0 gives equal one step; 0 would stay 0, which is why both callers force a zero seed to 1.

Adds the 20 bytes of the name buffer $EAB3-$EAC6 (the typed name as PETSCII, zero-padded, copied from $EA00 at $74BB) into $23, modulo 256. The number of check-register steps in account_encode ($90EE) and account_decode ($9155).

One step of the bouncing ball of the title's sing-along (called from the title loop at $6301, $6332, $6345 and $8E24; A, X and Y are saved in $EA6D-$EA6F and returned): sprite 0 on ($D015 = 1). At the start of each 16-step hop ($EA6B = 0), once the hold count $EA71 runs out, it reads the next byte of the script at $92BC through the pointer $EA69/$EA6A: below $80, bit 6 cleared, the X speed for the hop ($EA6C); $80 and above, a hold of (byte AND $7F) extra hops in place, and $BF (or $FF) also returns the ball to X = 0. At the end ($93E1) the pointer sticks on the last byte. Y moves by the 16 steps of $8EA7 (-3 up to +3, a parabola); X ($EA66, bit 8 in $EA68) wraps to 0 past $157. Writes sprites 0 and 1's X, Y and the X high bits in $D010.
Puts the sing-along ball back to the start (called from $6299 and $62FE): X = 0 ($EA66, $EA68), Y = $BA ($EA67), hop step $EA6B and hold $EA71 zero, script pointer $EA69/$EA6A = $92BC.

The sing-along ball's script, 293 bytes read one per hop by singalong_ball_step ($91C8): a byte below $80 is the X step per frame for one 16-frame hop (bit 6 ignored, so $40 is a hop on the spot), a byte of $80 or more holds the ball for (byte AND $7F) extra hops, and $BF also sends it back to the left edge. The last byte, $93E0, is $BF, re-read for ever once the song is over. The timing of the words on screen is not in this table.
The RTS music_play ($93F0) branches to at $93F2 when $47 bit 7 is set: the tune is paused and no SID register is written that frame.

Starts the tune again from its beginning on all three voices: zeroes each voice's track position $82-$84, pattern position $85-$87 and duration counter $88-$8A, so the next pass of music_play ($93F0) reads the first note. Called when a voice's track ends and $20 is non-zero ($942E), and from $628E, $62FB, $7ACF, $8DA6.

The music player, called once a frame from the raster IRQ ($8FBA) and from $632F. Returns at once while $47 bit 7 is set. For each voice (X = 2..0; SID register offset $A2B4,x = 0, 7, 14, kept in $E1): on every fourth frame ($08 AND 3 = 0) it counts the voice's duration $88,x down (a negative $88 means stopped) and, when it runs out, reads the next event: the pattern number from the voice's track list ($A2B7/$A2BA,x at position $82,x; $FF ends the track, which stops the voice or, when $20 is set, restarts the tune via $93E2), the pattern address from $A75B, and at position $85,x the event byte (bits 0-4 duration, bit 6 a rest with the gate off, bit 7 an extra byte follows: low nibble the instrument $94,x, high nibble the volume for $D418, 15 meaning a fade computed from 109 minus voice 1's track position, halved when $20 is set) and the note number, whose frequency comes from the table at $A1F4. Instrument settings (pulse width, control, attack/decay, sustain/release) come from the 8-byte records at $A7EF. Between events it drops the gate unless bit 5 of the event was set and silences the envelope at the end of the note, and on every frame it adds vibrato (depth $A7F4 of the instrument, a triangle from $08) to notes longer than 4. Voice 3 is left alone while $98 is set (music_voice3_busy, $9593).

Returns A = $FF (Z clear) when the music player must not write the SID for the voice it is on: $98 is non-zero and the voice index $EA75 is 2 (SID voice 3, which the game's sound effects use); otherwise A = 0. Called four times from music_play ($93F0).
Clears the eight sprites' software state (called from $7AD5, $88C6 and $8AFA): positions $A0-$AF, targets $B0-$BF, shape numbers $2B-$32, and the walking frame $77.

Clears the text screen rows 0-23 at $5400-$57BF to character 0 and their colour RAM $D800-$DBBF to 0 (black), leaving the bottom row with its scroller alone; $37 = 0. When the game state $3A is $11 or more, colours row 22 ($DB70-$DB96, 39 cells) white, the line the play screens print messages on. Called from nine places, among them init_game_vars.

Draws one character row (Y = 0-3) of the building in city-map slot X (0-29) (called from $7B18, which draws all 30 slots, and $89D6): five characters from the shape table $3F2D at kind offset $A855[$EA28,x] (20 per kind) plus row offset $A85D[Y] (5 per row), to the slot's screen address from the split table $A861/$A87F plus Y*40. Skips rows 0-1 of slots 0-3 and 29 and rows 2-3 of slots 16-21. X and Y are preserved.

Subtracts the BCD amount $25 (high), $24, $23 from the balance $57 (high), $58, $59 in decimal mode; if the balance would go below zero it becomes 0. Called from $7652 and $791D (buying the car and the equipment) and $8983 (the $4000 charge that follows the message $4000 DAMAGE, set up at $8974-$8981). The online cheat POKE 38454,96 turns its first byte into RTS: tested in the simulator, the hearse is then free and the balance stays $10000; by the same token the $4000 damage charge at $8983 is not taken either (live, work/verify/t20-poke-mm.js: $10000 stayed $10000 through a stomp, $6000 without the poke).

Compares the balance $57/$58/$59 with the BCD amount $25/$24/$23 by a decimal subtraction whose result is thrown away: carry set when the balance is at least the amount. Called from $7646 and $7918, before a purchase.

Adds the BCD amount $25 (high), $24, $23 to the balance $57, $58, $59; on overflow past 999999 sets $57 and $58 to $99 and leaves $59 as it is. Called from $8801, $89F7 and $8C6E (payments during play).

Prints the next line of the sing-along lyrics on screen row 22 ($5770) (called from the title loop at $6382): characters from the pointer $21/$22, a space becoming character 0 and letters losing $40 to become screen codes, up to $0D or 40 characters, the rest of the row blanked, and the pointer advanced past the line. The end mark $FF sets the pointer back to $6443, the start of the lyrics, and prints nothing.

Reads the joystick in control port 1: port A all outputs and high ($DC02 = $DC00 = $FF, so no keyboard row is selected), port B inputs ($DC03 = 0), then $33 = $DC01 AND $1F (bits 0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right, 4 fire, active low; $1F = at rest). Any movement or fire clears $45 and $46, the counters that blank the screen when nobody plays. Called from $6329, $6396, $7061.

Keyboard scan (called from $632C and $7070). Does nothing if $DC01 or $DC00 read anything but $FF with all rows released (a joystick in either port is active). Otherwise tests all 64 keys, index = column (the $DC01 bit, mask $374B) * 8 + row (the $DC00 value $3753), and keeps in $19 the lowest index held whose entry in the key table $389E is not $21 ($FF when none): F1 is $20, F3 $28, RUN/STOP $3F. The key's character from $389E goes to $17 and $18 and clears $45/$46, but only when it differs from $18 (no auto-repeat); none held, or a key whose entry is $2F (the function keys, RUN/STOP), sets $18 = 0 instead.

The scrolling bottom row (called from the raster IRQ at $8EA1 and $8EED, on every screen): unless $02 has bit 7 set and bit 6 clear, counts the 10-bit position $04/$05 down by one; then writes 40 characters of the 128-character loop at $3624 (the Activision logo characters, PRESS F1 OR F3 TO START, GHOSTBUSTERS, DESIGNED BY DAVID CRANE, COPYRIGHT 1984) starting at character 127 - (position / 8), to row 24 at $57C0, spaces as 0 and codes of $40 and above AND $3F. The fine scroll (position AND 7) is set by bottom_scroller_logo_sprite ($97A1).

Bottom-band raster work (called from the IRQ at $8ECE and $8F6E): puts sprite 7 (shape $3B, colour 2, Y = $F2) at X = position $04/$05 minus $3B8 so that it travels with the Activision logo in the scrolling row, enabling it alone ($D015 = $80) or hiding it when that X is $200 or more; waits for raster $F2, then sets the fine scroll ($D016 low bits = $04 AND 7, 38 columns off, multicolour off) and clears $D011's bits 6-7; makes sprite 7 single-colour and behind the characters and, for raster lines $F4-$FB, changes its colour line by line from $3714 (8 8 7 7 5 5 6 0: orange, yellow, green, blue), the rainbow stripes of the logo; then puts $D01C and $D01B back.
Replaces a leading ASCII '0' in $23 by 0 (a blank): used after bcd_to_ascii ($99B7) at $71D7 and $7280 so that a two-digit figure prints as " 7" rather than "07".
Restores sprites 4-7 from the copies kept in $EA4E-$EA55 and $C4-$C7 (called from $8986 and $89FA): targets $B8-$BF = $EA4E-$EA55 and shape numbers $2F-$32 = $C4-$C7.

Sends sprite X/2 back to its starting place (called from $7BCB after a sprite has reached its goal and PK has gone up by 100, and from $8242): $28 = how many of $C4-$C7 are non-zero; the saved position $EA46,x/$EA47,x and saved target $EA56,x/$EA57,x are set from $37B3,x/$37B4,x and $37C3,x/$37C4,x, and when the game state $3A is $12 the live position $A0,x and target $B0,x too. Ends with CLD for its caller, which ran pk_add_hundreds in decimal mode.

Adds A hundreds to the city's PK energy, the four BCD digits $5A (low two) and $5B (high two): sets decimal mode and clears carry, then pk_add_hundreds_carry ($9897). Called with A = 1 at $7BC8 and A = 3 at $73DF.

PK energy addition with decimal mode and carry already set by the caller ($7409 adds 0 with the carry from incrementing $5A, the steady rise): $5B = $5B + A + C. A carry out of $5B caps PK at 9999 ($5A = $5B = $99). When the thousands digit has changed and PK is now 5000 or more, it picks a building: from the random byte $06, X = its low nibble raised to at least 4, stepping on until the map slot $EA28,x holds a building and X is not 10; then $80 = X and that building's state $C8,x = $C8. Tested live: taking PK from 4998 past 5000 marked building 9. Ends with CLD.

For each man (sprite 5 at $AA/$AB into $23, sprite 6 at $AC/$AD into $24): the X his proton stream reaches at the Slimer's height, the man's X plus (man's Y - Slimer's Y $A9) / 4, negated when the man's shape number $30/$31 minus $0E is odd (facing left). Used by slimer_side_of_streams ($9918) and streams_confine_slimer ($992B); called from $858F and $9ABC.

Records on which side of each stream the Slimer is: for X = 1, 0, $7E,x = $FF when the Slimer's X $A8 is less than the stream's X $23,x, else 0. Called from $8592 and by streams_confine_slimer when a stream is out of reach.

Keeps the Slimer between the streams (called from $85A2): with the streams' X in $23/$24 ($98EB) and the men's Y in $25/$26, if the two streams are within 6 pixels of each other the Slimer's direction becomes 6 (straight down). For each stream: if the man is $60 or more below the Slimer the stream does not reach it, and the routine re-records the sides and returns ($9918); otherwise a Slimer that has moved across the stream from the side recorded in $7E,x is put back on the stream's X and turned away from it (direction 0, right, or 4, left). The direction is stored in $7D.

Moves the Slimer (sprite 4, $A8/$A9) one step in direction $7D (0-7: right, up-right, up, up-left, left, down-left, down, down-right; steps $A9B8/$A9C0,x) and keeps it in the box X $48-$8F, Y $30-$6F: at an edge it is put back inside and the direction is turned half round (+4). The target $B8/$B9 is set to the new position. Called from $9AB9.
Splits the BCD byte in A into two ASCII digits: $23 = the tens ('0'-'9'), $24 = the units. Called from $71D4, $71E4, $71EE, $727D, $728D (the play screen's figures).

Starts one of the ten play-screen messages, X = 0-9 (split pointer table $B3F4/$B3FE: NO EMPTY TRAPS, BACKUP MEN OUT OF ACTION, NO BAIT, BACKPACKS DISCHARGED, MARSHMALLOW ALERT, $4000 DAMAGE, MAYOR AWARDS $2000, CAR LOADED TO CAPACITY, CROSSED THE STREAMS, GO TO ZUUL), unless one is already showing ($4B non-zero): copies it to $E900 as screen codes (space to 0, letters minus $40) with its $FF end mark, counts its characters in $4A, sets $4B = 1. Called from eleven places.
Z set when sprite X/2's position $A0,x/$A1,x equals its target $B0,x/$B1,x. Called from $887F (and $87B1, $8912, $8B31, $8B51 by address).
Sets bit 0 of the Slimer's shape number $2F from bit 3 of the pass counter $09, so it alternates between two shapes every eight passes. Called from $8786 and $886F.

Puts the trap (sprite 7, $AE/$AF and its target $BE/$BF) at the first man's feet: X = his X $AA minus 6, plus 12 when he faces right ($77 bit 0 clear), Y = his Y $AB minus 7. Called from $8502 and $889E.

Arranges sprites 0-3 as a column above the trap (sprite 7 at $AE/$AF), called from $86B0 and $875B: steps the counter $79 through 0-5 and sets the four shapes $2B-$2E to $A9CA-$A9CD plus $79; all four at the trap's X; from the height counter $7A (mirrored above $48 as $9C - $7A, so it grows and then shrinks) the sprites' Y are spread upwards from the trap's Y - $15. Live: it ran 129 times in 300 frames after the trap was sprung from agent5-beams.json (work/verify/t19-letters-trap.js).

During a bust (called from $8525, $8531 and $8568): if the building's state $C8,x (X = the building $6E) still has both bits 2-3 set, returns. Otherwise blanks the Slimer's shape ($2F = 0) and, unless $7C is set, discards its caller's return address, sets the game state $3A = $1F and jumps to $8823.

The Slimer's per-pass work during a bust (called from $8522, $852E, $8565, $859B and $86A0): sprite 4 in front of the background when $6D bit 1 is set, behind it otherwise ($D01B bit 4); moves it (slimer_move $9972), recomputes the streams' X at its height ($98EB), and every fourth pass ($09 AND 3 = 0) turns its direction $7D by the random bit $06 AND 1 and sets its shape $2F to $0A plus another random bit. Live (work/verify/t16-intensifier.js): $D01B = $10 without the image intensifier, $00 with it; the frame pictures show the Slimer cut by a window without it.

Fire-button edge test: A = the fire bit of the joystick ($33 AND $10), compared with the previous one in $11 (Z set when unchanged), then stored in $11. Called from $7E74, $850F, $8541, $857E and $865E.

Moves all eight sprites one pixel toward their targets: step_sprite_toward_target ($9C25) with A = 2 for X = $0E, $0C ... 0 (sprites 7 to 0). Called from ten places between $84F7 and $88EB ($84F7, $852B, $8562, $85A5, $86A3, $8704, $8794, $887A, $889B, $88EB), the code that runs the scene at a haunted building.

Moves the target of man X/2 (sprite 5 at X = 0, sprite 6 at X = 2; $BA,x/$BB,x) one pixel for the joystick $33: right +X, left -X, down +Y, up -Y. Called from $84FC, $8536, $856D and $8B71. A second entry at $9AF1 takes the direction bits in A instead (from $85CA).

Second entry of man_target_from_stick ($9AEF): the direction bits come in A instead of from the joystick $33 (active low: bit 3 clear moves the target of man X/2 right, bit 2 left, bit 1 down, bit 0 up), kept in $24. Called from $85CA.
Keeps the target of man X/2 ($BA,x/$BB,x) on the pavement: X between $20 and $8C, Y between $AA and $C8. Called from $84FF, $8539, $8570 and $85CD.

Walking animation of both men: $23 = A, the shape number to use when standing, then animate_man ($9B44) for the second man (X = 1, sprite 6) and the first (X = 0, sprite 5). Called from $84F4, $853E, $8877 and $8898.

Walking animation of man X (0 or 1; Y = 2X indexes his sprite's X/Y): on every other pass, while his X differs from his target's, bit 0 of $77,x becomes his facing (1 when the target is to the left) and his step ($77,x bits 1-2) advances. His shape $30,x is then $23 OR facing when he stands on his target, else $77,x + $0E. Called from animate_both_men and from $857B, $88E2, $8B45, $8B65.

Turns the name as typed, LAST,FIRST, into FIRST LAST in the text buffer $EA14: clears $EA14-$EA27, copies what follows the comma in $EAB3-$EAC6, adds a space after it, then the leading letters A-Z of the name (stopping at the comma or any non-letter), ends it with $FF and selects message $80 (the buffer, select_message $9BEE). A name with no comma gives a space and the name. Called from $8C96 and $8D06 (the end-of-game texts).

Selects message A for the interview and end-of-game text engine: $EA76 = 1 when bit 7 of A is set (read at $72E3), else 0; $4D = A; the text pointer $4E/$4F from the table $B36D at 2*A (bit 7 dropped): 0 the buffer $EA14, 1 the interview's opening, 2 DO YOU HAVE AN ACCOUNT?, 4 WHAT IS YOUR ACCOUNT NUMBER?, 5 INVALID ACCOUNT NUMBER., 6 the vehicle page, ... $11 YOUR NEW ACCOUNT NUMBER IS. Called from 29 places.
Carry set when $23 <= A < $24, clear otherwise. Called from $7DBC, $7DD1, $81C2, $86EF.
Compares all eight sprites' positions $A0-$AF with their targets $B0-$BF: Z set (and A = 0) when every sprite has arrived, Z clear at the first difference. Called from $7860 and $7900.
step_sprite_toward_target ($9C25) with A = 3: at most 2 pixels a pass. Called from $774B and $80A2.

Moves sprite X/2's position $A0,x/$A1,x toward its target $B0,x/$B1,x, each axis on its own, by the distance or A - 1, whichever is less. The distance is taken as an unsigned difference, so when the target lies below the position (a negative difference) the step is always A - 1, and a target one or two pixels away is overshot and approached again from the other side. Called from sprite code at $7C97, $8929, $8A07, $8B2C, $8B4C, $8B6C and eight times a pass by $9AE3.
The distance |$B1,x - $A1,x| between sprite X/2's Y and its target's Y, in A. Nothing calls it: no JSR, JMP or address to $9C76 in the image (byte scan), and it never ran in the simulator.
Empties the typed-line buffer: the input index $50 = 1, so the next character goes to $EA00. Called from $74B5, $74D2, $74FF, $75B9, $760F, before each answer is typed.
Stores the typed character A at $E9FF + $50 (the buffer $EA00 on), advances $50 and echoes it through print_char ($9C8F). Called from $736D and $7383 (the typing code of the interview and shop).

Prints one character of the text engine at column $38, row $39 of the screen at $5400 (row address from $AAE5, row * 10, times 4), in colour $48 in the matching colour RAM: 0 prints nothing; $80 and above sets the column to A AND $3F; $0D moves to column 1 of the next row; otherwise a space becomes 0, codes of $40 and above lose $40, and the column advances. When $15 is set and $48 is 0, a space at column 32 or beyond also starts a new row (word wrap). Called from $733D and input_add_char.

Sets the balance to $10,000 ($57 = 1, $58 = $59 = 0). Nothing calls it: no JSR, JMP or address to $9CF1 in the image (byte scan), and it never ran in the simulator; the interview does the same inline at $74EA.

Turns the typed account number at $EA00 into four bytes: for up to eight characters, stopping at a 0 byte, the low nibble of each is shifted into the 32-bit $23 (high) ... $26 (low), so a shorter number is right-aligned with leading zeros. The character itself is not checked: '8' gives 8, '9' 9, 'A' 1, 'L' $C The line input lets letters through: LEFTY typed as the number for the name LEFTY packed to $000C5649 and gave $860000, as the cheat lists say (live, work/verify/t19-letters-trap.js). Called from $7505, which copies $23-$26 to $EAC7-$EACA for account_decode ($9155).

Writes the balance $57/$58/$59 as text into $EA14: a '0', the six BCD digits and $FF; leading zeros become spaces (keeping the last digit) and a '$' goes in front of the first digit left, so $002500 becomes "   $2500". Called from $72AC, $73AD, $75A2, $8CB0, $8D4F, $8D71; trim_leading_spaces ($9063) usually follows.

Writes A bytes from $23 on as digit characters, each nibble OR $30 (a nibble above 9 would give : to ?), into the text buffer from $EA14, ending with $FF: the entry of bytes_to_digits ($9D51) with Y = 0. Called only with A = 4 from $8CDF, to print the new account number $EAC7-$EACA as eight digits, each 0-7 by construction.
Writes $27 bytes from $23 on as two digit characters each (high nibble then low, OR $30) into $EA14 from position Y, then $FF. BCD bytes give decimal digits.

Replaces the leading '0' characters of the text in $EA14 by spaces, stopping at the first other character, at a '.', or at the last digit before the $FF end, so a zero still prints one 0. Returns X = the position of the first character kept.
Copies 1536 bytes (six pages) from the pointer $0D/$0E to $0F/$10, ascending: copy_pages ($9D9A) with X = 5, Y = 0. Called from $7AC8, $7AFE, $82D5 (screens and character sets).
Copies X + 1 pages from ($0D) to ($0F), starting at offset Y, ascending, stepping the pointers' high bytes. Entered at $841C with X = 1 to copy two pages of facade characters to $5BD0.

Copies downwards from ($0D),Y to ($0F),Y: Y counts down to 0 on each page, then both high bytes go down one, for X + 1 pages. Called from $82FA with X = 3, Y = $47: the building screen's 840 characters from $2698 (or $1880 for building 10) to $5400-$5747.

Ten rate masks, one per thousand of PK energy ($5B's high digit, read at $72C4 into $3C): $3F $1F $0F $07 $03 then $01. $73F7 raises PK by 1 when the pass counter $09 AND ($3C OR $0F) is 0, so PK creeps up once every 64 passes below 1000, every 32 below 2000 and every 16 from there on; $7C87 uses $3C as it is.
GHOSTBUSTERS in PETSCII, 12 characters, written by $8425 (AND $3F, in red) to row 8 of the building screen at $554D when the building is 17: the sign over GHQ's door.

Four colours for a building's walls (orange $0A replaced by entry $A1C0,x AND 3): $0A light red, $08 orange, $09 brown, $0D light green. Read at $8305 while $8328 copies the building's colour map to $D800.
Four sets of 16 bytes, the bitmaps of characters $4D-$4E, copied to $5A68 by $8447 for bits 2-3 of the building's $A1C0 entry. Set 0 ($9DD4-$9DE3) is never read, because a 0 there skips the copy.

Character bitmaps for the building's windows, 112 bytes (14 characters, $66-$73) copied to $5B30 by $8394: from offset $9F18[n] for window style n of the building's $A1C0 entry (bits 4-5): style 1 uses $9E14-$9E83 and style 2 $9E5C-$9ECB, overlapping by 40 bytes.
Character codes of one window, 24 per style (4 wide, 6 tall), written by $8373 at the offsets $9EFC into each of the four windows: style 1 at $9ECC, style 2 at $9EE4 (offsets from $9F14).
The screen offsets of a window's 24 cells, 4 across and 6 down (0-3, $28-$2B, ... $C8-$CB), added at $836C to the window's start ($5430 plus 6 columns per window).

Per window style (0-3), the offset of its character codes in window_char_codes ($9ECC): -, 0, $18, $30. Style 0 means no change; style 3 is used by no building in $A1C0 and would read the offsets table.
Per window style (0-3), the offset of its bitmaps in window_char_bitmaps ($9E14): -, 0, $48, $B8. Style 3 is used by no building.

Low bytes of the lower-facade character maps, per style 0-3 from bits 6-7 of the building's $A1C0 entry, read at $83AF (high bytes at $9F20): -, $9F2C, $A008, $A0E4. Each map is 10 rows of 22 characters written at $5520 on (rows 7-16, columns 8-29), in colour 9.
High bytes of the lower-facade character maps (lows at $9F1C), read at $83B4: -, $9F, $A0, $A0.
Low bytes of the addresses of the two pages of characters that go with each lower-facade style, read at $8406 (high bytes at $9F28): -, $3050, $3138, $3208; copied to $5BD0 by copy_pages ($9D9A).
High bytes of the lower-facade character pages (lows at $9F24), read at $840B: -, $30, $31, $32.

The theme tune's 71 patterns (numbers 0-70; 38, 39, 58, 59 are null in pattern_ptrs), 852 bytes, packed back to back. Bit 5 ties the note (no gate-off, $9503). $FF ends a pattern. Parsed by $9446-$94F4.

Addresses of the 28 text pages, by page number x 2, read at $9BFD/$9C02 by $9BEE (A = page, bit 7 set also sets $EA76) into the typewriter pointer $4E/$4F. Page 0 is at $EA14 and page 12 at $EB00 (built in RAM at run time), pages 20-23 are the car options at $38DE-$39B6, page 19 is the empty page at $B3A9, the rest are in this range.
High bytes of the text_page_ptrs words, read as $B36E,x at $9C02.
Text page number of each vehicle's options (20-23), read at $7609 and passed to $9BEE when SPACE steps through the cars.
Text page 19: a lone $FF, a page that ends at once.
'GHQ' in screen codes, written under the GHQ block of the city map ($572E) by $7B60.

Two joystick readings made up by the game, $07 (right) and $0B (left); $85BF reads the first and third (X = 2, 0), EORs them with $0C to swap left and right when needed and ORs in the player's $33, then man_target_from_bits ($9AF1, from $85CA) moves the man. The middle byte is not read.
Status message 9: GO TO ZUUL( SNEAK PAST THE MARSHMALLOW MAN AND CLOSE THE PORTAL... , shown by $99CC through status_msg_lo/hi; '(' is drawn as '!'.
Low bytes of the ten status-line messages shown by $99CC (X = message): $3A16, $3A40, $3A78, $3A89, $3AB0, $3AC5, $3B21, $3B5F, $3B80 and txt_go_to_zuul.
High bytes of the ten status-line message addresses, read at $99D5.

The run-length packed sprite shapes: the cold start's unpacker at $610B reads from here to $BFF7 and writes 3,800 bytes to $4000-$4ED7, sprite shapes 0-59 (shape n at $4000 + n x 64). A byte $11 is followed by a count of zero bytes to write (0 meaning 256); every other byte is copied. Shape 59 gets only its first 8 rows.
Second kilobyte of packed_sprites ($B408-$BFF7): the run-length stream of the sprite shapes continues.
Third part of packed_sprites, to $BFF7 where the unpacker's end test at $610D stops.

Eight bytes after the end of packed_sprites that the unpacker never reads (it stops when the source reaches $BFF8). They continue shape 59's pattern (FF FF F8, FF FF F8, F8 6D), so the stream was cut short or this is leftover; nothing else reads them.
Named only by the dead tape loader: STA $BFFF at $CE5B, which never runs. The game itself neither reads nor writes this byte; its value $6D is leftover.

The conversion's hand-over to the game, called once by the stub at $033C after the one-file load (orientation.md): SEI; masks every CIA 1 and CIA 2 interrupt ($7F to $DC0D and $DD0D) and reads both interrupt registers to clear what is pending; copies the 256 bytes at $C830 to $0300-$03FF and zeroes $0200-$02FF, putting back the two pages the load had to overwrite; then JMP $6000, the game's cold start, never returning. Nothing in the game calls it (no instruction names $C800).
Fourteen $FF bytes between oneload_handover and its page image; no instruction names them and no simulator run reads them. Filler.

Page image copied to $0300-$03FF by oneload_handover ($C811): $0300-$0313 zero, $0314/$0315 = $0A00, $0316/$0317 = $2F0B, $0318/$0319 = $352D, then 230 bytes that look like graphics (runs of $AA, $0F, $03, $BA...). It is what the conversion found in that page. Nothing in the game uses it: no instruction names $0300-$03FF, the IRQ and NMI go through $FFFE/$FFFA with the KERNAL banked out, and the simulator's read maps (title to the end of a game) show no read of $0300-$03FF.

A turbo tape loader left in memory, never executed in this image: no instruction jumps to $CE00-$CED5 (only $CF80, itself never reached) and the simulator never ran it. What it would do: $00 = $2F, $01 = $06 (cassette motor on), screen off ($D011 = $0B), NMI vector $0318 = $CEC1 (RESTORE while loading wipes memory), CIA 2 timer A latch $0118; syncs on 256 one-bits, then a zero, then the byte $33; reads a 2-byte start address into the store at $CE5B (self-modified), a 2-byte end address into $CED8/$CED9, then data bytes up to and including the end address with an XOR checksum in $CED7; a matching checksum byte calls the KERNAL at $FC93, $FDA3 (IOINIT) and $FD15, CLI and returns; a mismatch goes to tape_load_fail ($CEC1). Which program this loader originally fetched is not known.
store address, self-modified from the block header at $CE43/$CE49 and stepped at $CE8B/$CE93

Operand of the dead loader's STA $BFFF at $CE5B, the load address: written from the header at $CE43, compared with the end address at $CE64, and stepped at $CE8B. The loop from here stores each byte, updates the checksum, and stops when this address reaches tape_end_address.
High byte of the dead loader's store address (header byte 2, $CE49), stepped at $CE93 when the low byte wraps, compared at $CE6C.
Part of the dead tape loader: reads 8 bits, most significant first, through tape_read_bit into $CED6 and returns the byte in A.

Part of the dead tape loader: waits for a pulse on the cassette read line (CIA 1 interrupt flag bit 4, the FLAG input, in $DC0D), then shifts CIA 2's timer A underflow flag (bit 0 of $DD0D) into the carry: 1 when more than $0118 cycles have passed since the previous pulse, a long pulse; restarts the timer ($DD0E = $11) and flips the border colour (EOR 5) for the familiar loading stripes.

Part of the dead tape loader, reached on a checksum mismatch and installed as the NMI (RESTORE) handler at $CE10: stores $02 into every byte from $0202 upward (pointer $9E/$9F) flashing the border, then JMP $FCE2 (the KERNAL's reset). The fill reaches its own loop at $CEC7 on the way, and $02 is a JAM opcode, so in practice it would stop the processor before the reset. An anti-tamper wipe.
Dead tape loader variable: the byte being assembled by tape_read_byte ($CE9E ROL, $CEA4 read).
Dead tape loader variable: XOR of the data bytes loaded (cleared at $CE29, updated at $CE5E-$CE61, compared with the block's last byte at $CE78).
Dead tape loader variable, 2 bytes: the block's end address from its header ($CE4F, $CE55), compared with the store address at $CE67/$CE6F.
High byte of tape_end_address (header byte 4, written at $CE55, compared at $CE6F).

Four calls never executed and named by no instruction: JSR $CE00 (tape_turbo_loader), JSR $0A00, JSR $CE00, JSR $0E00, then a $00 byte (BRK): load a block and run it, twice. Together with the $0A00 IRQ vector in page3_image it looks like the remains of the original tape loading sequence; what $0A00 and $0E00 held then is not known (in this image they are part of the game).

Six pages holding characters $40-$FF of the character set at $5A00-$5FFF, that is the car picture with the bought equipment painted in: saved there when leaving the shop (st10_map_setup, $7AC8 through $9D96) and copied back to $5A00 at the start of each drive ($8007-$8027), because the map's character set replaces it in between. Runtime storage: the image's bytes here are only the machine's power-on pattern.
Second part of car_charset_save ($E000-$E5FF): its pages 5 and 6, characters $C0-$FF of the saved car picture.

256-byte table built by cold_start ($6074-$6088): for each byte, every multicolour pixel pair with either bit set made %11, so AND with it keeps a shape's pixels and AND with its inverse clears the background under them. Read by shop_paint_item_in_car ($79EE) to cut the item's shape into the car picture.

256-byte table built by cold_start ($606C): each byte with its four 2-bit pixels in reverse order, a left-right mirror of multicolour graphics. Read by build_mirrored_sprites ($6156-$6183) for the sprites that face both ways and by build_car_charset ($76A2) for the car's right half.
