16 bytes, a copy of the map sprites' targets $B0-$BF (two bytes per sprite): from $37C3 at st10_map_setup ($7AA7) and reset_sprite_home ($9882); the logo's own position at map_building_under_logo ($7D28/$7D32); compared with the positions by st12_city_map ($7BB7/$7BBE) to see a Roamer arrive; restored into $B0 by st11_draw_map ($7B9B).
Second byte of sprite 0's saved target in map_sprite_target_save, written at $7D32 and $988C, compared at $7BBE.

Saved targets of sprites 2 and 3 within map_sprite_target_save: set with the targets $B4-$B7 by st12_city_map ($7C1F, sending them to Zuul) and by map_gatekeepers_wander ($7E3E, the next street crossing).
Second byte of each of sprites 2 and 3's saved targets, set at $7C27 and $7E4F.
Sprites 4-7's saved targets within map_sprite_target_save: $8A1D copies these 8 bytes back into $B8-$BF (the Roamers' targets) and returns to the map, state $12.
Sing-along ball: X position, low byte (bit 8 in ball_x_high $EA68); stepped by the hop's speed in singalong_ball_step ($9251, $9267), wraps to 0 past $157, zeroed by singalong_ball_reset ($929E).
Sing-along ball: Y position, moved by the 16-step bounce table at $8EA7 ($9239-$923C); $BA after singalong_ball_reset ($92A3).
Sing-along ball: bit 8 of the X position (with ball_x), ORed into the sprite X high bits for sprites 0 and 1 ($9283); zeroed by singalong_ball_reset.

Sing-along ball: pointer to the next byte of the hop script at $92BC, low byte here and high byte at $EA6A; stepped at $9215/$921A, set by singalong_ball_reset ($92B3/$92B8), sticks on the last byte ($93E1).
High byte of ball_script_ptr (the hop script pointer), stepped at $921A when the low byte wraps.
Sing-along ball: step 0-15 within the current hop, the index into the bounce table ($91D6); a new script byte is read when it is 0. Zeroed by singalong_ball_reset.
Sing-along ball: X speed for the current hop, the script byte with bit 6 cleared ($9212), added to ball_x each step ($924E).
singalong_ball_step's saved A, X and Y ($EA6D, $EA6F, $EA6E: stored at $91C8-$91CE, restored at $9292-$9298). $EA70 after them is named by no instruction and never touched in the simulator: unused.
singalong_ball_step's saved Y ($91CE, restored at $9298).
singalong_ball_step's saved X ($91CB, restored at $9295). The byte after it, $EA70, is unused.
Sing-along ball: hops still to wait in place, from a script byte of $80 or more (AND $7F, $920D); counted down at $91DB; zeroed by singalong_ball_reset ($92AE).

Scratch byte with two users: pk_add_hundreds_carry keeps the PK thousands digit (high nibble of $5B) before the addition in it ($989C) to see it change ($98A8), and saves X in it while picking a building ($98B1/$98DD); $861B-$8629 use it as a count of 64 raster interrupts, calling $9080 on each.

$FF on a PAL machine, $00 on NTSC: set by draw_title_screen ($62BD) from the last raster line; read by title_frame_work ($6338) and the raster IRQ ($8EE0) to run the tune's tick twice in one frame of eight on PAL.

pk_add_hundreds_carry's search index when PK reaches a new thousand at 5000 or more: starts at the random byte $06 ($98B6) and is incremented ($98CA) until map_slot_table holds a building at (index AND $0F, at least 4) that is not Zuul (10).
The voice music_play is working on, 0-2 ($93F6); music_voice3_busy ($9599) compares it with 2 so that the music leaves SID voice 3 to the sound effects while $98 is set.
Text colour flag of the current message: select_message sets 1 when bit 7 of the message number is set, else 0 ($9BF6); frame_type_message copies it to $48, the colour it prints with ($72E3).
Busting-scene flag, meaning not settled: 1 at $8A7C (the routine at $8A6A that also places sprites through $AA/$AB and $BA/$BB), $FF at $8AC2 after a man is lost, 0 at $8B58; tested at $8B1F.
Busting-scene counter: 2 at $8A5E; $8AE1 decrements it together with the men-left count $3D; $8B0B branches away when it is 0. Its partner is $EA79.
Busting-scene counter: 2 at $8A61; $8AB2 decrements it with the men-left count $3D and then plays speech phrase 3 ($8AB9); $8B10 branches away when it is 0. Its partner is $EA78.

Flag that makes two points of the play code speak: set to 1 at $86D2 and to $3B at $8C80, cleared at $8658, $8C8B and $8CFB; when non-zero, $8744 plays speech phrase 2 (just after adding 300 PK at $873F) and $8D18 plays phrase 3.

Sound-effect interpreter on SID voice 3 ($3BE9 on): the command byte just read from the effect's data ($3C34); its low nibble picks the handler from the tables at $3D83/$3D92 ($3C3C), and handlers read it back ($3C5B, $3CC5).
Sound-effect interpreter: X saved while fetching the next data byte through ($E7) ($3C61/$3C6E).

Sound-effect interpreter: the voice 3 control value with the gate bit clear ($3D0B, from the table at $3D74), written to $D412 to release the note when the duration reaches the release point ($3BFA) and with the gate set to start one ($3C81). Zeroed when an effect starts ($3D3F).

Sound-effect interpreter: a frequency wobble; each tick it is negated and added to the current frequency into $D40F ($3C06-$3C17), so the pitch alternates up and down. Set from a command's high nibble ($3CE4), zeroed when an effect starts ($3D42).

Sound-effect interpreter: repeat counter of a loop command ($3CCC): decremented at $3CCF, and while it is not 0 the data pointer ($E7) is moved back by the byte that follows. Set from a command's high nibble ($3CEC).
Sound-effect interpreter: the duration value at which the note's gate is released ($3BF5 compares sfx_duration with it); $FF (never) when an effect starts ($3D4B).

Sound-effect interpreter: ticks left in the current step, counted down each tick ($3BED); at 0 the next command is read ($3C03). Set from the table at $3D5C by a command's high nibble ($3C7A), 1 when an effect starts ($3D2C), 0 to stop ($3BE3, $3C53).

The value last written to $D418 (volume and filter mode) by music_play ($9483), kept so that it can be put back after the RUN/STOP pause silences the SID (frame_pause_key $70CE) and after speech ($8E39), and by frame_type_message ($730B-$7314).

Sound-effect interpreter: voice 3's frequency high byte ($D40F), set from the note table at $3DFA ($3CA0), moved by sweeps ($3C21/$3C27), relative steps ($3D1A) and the wobble ($3C14). $EA85 after it is named by no instruction: unused.

Sound-effect interpreter: frequency sweep direction, positive = up one step per tick, negative = down ($3C1A-$3C27); set by a command ($3CC8), zeroed when an effect starts ($3D45). $EA85 after it is named by no instruction and never touched in the simulator.
Sound-effect interpreter: the note number of the last note command ($3C90), the index into the frequency tables $3E5A/$3DFA; written only.

Set to 0 by draw_title_screen ($62D4) and read by nothing (no instruction names it, and no simulator run reads it). The disassembler's KERNAL name for $EA87 (scan keyboard) does not apply: here it is RAM.
A flag with no effect: 0 at $877E, 1 at $87C6, and the only read, LDA $EA88 / BEQ $8837 at $8832, branches to the next instruction either way. A left-over.
Sing-along ball: the script byte just read ($91F1), kept so that BIT can test its bit 6 ($91F5).

40 bytes: the bottom screen row at $57C0 (row 24 of the $5400 screen), saved and blanked by the speech routine $8DB9 when $20 is 0, as on the title ($8DDE-$8DE7), and put back after the phrase ($8E6A-$8E6F).
The function key that started the game: $20 for F1, $28 for F3 (title_frame_work $639F); zeroed by nmi_restore_handler ($6433); read by st00_interview_start ($747E) to skip the interview on F3.

The player's name as typed (LAST,FIRST), 20 bytes of PETSCII padded with zeros, copied from line_input_buffer by st01_name_entered ($74C0); summed by account_name_sum ($91BC) for the account number's check, and turned into FIRST LAST by build_first_last_name ($9BA3-$9BD0). It survives RESTORE, which is what lets F3 reuse it.

The account number, 4 bytes, one octal digit in each nibble: filled from the typed digits by st03_account_number ($750E-$751D) or by account_encode ($9114-$9149) at a win; read by account_decode ($915F) and printed at the end of a winning game ($8CC9-$8CD8). $EAC7 is the lowest byte.
Second byte of account_digits (written at $7513 and $9117, shifted at $912D/$9147, printed at $8CCE).
Third byte of account_digits (written at $7518 and $911A, shifted at $912A/$9144, printed at $8CD3).
Fourth and highest byte of account_digits (written at $751D and $911D, shifted at $9127/$9141, printed at $8CD8); account_decode reads its high nibble first.

121 bytes that cold_start fills with 120 spaces ($20) and an $FF end mark ($60E9-$60F7), the shape of a text buffer; no other instruction names $EB00-$EB78, and none of the simulator runs (title, interview, shop, map, drive, bust, Zuul, the winning ending) reads it. Initialised but unused in this version.

The speech player's waveform buffer, 128 bytes of $D418 values times two (a sample is written as 2 x volume, 0-$1E, and halved by LSR when played): the decoders write the next chunk into the half not playing ($00-$3F or $40-$7F, chosen by bit 6 of speech_play_start), and speech_crossfade writes blends into $20-$3F or $60-$7F. Played by the NMI handlers at $F083/$F0A4 through their self-modified LDA $F000. Runtime storage: the image holds whatever the last decode left ($0E/$10 bytes, one-bit samples).

The speech player's entry point, JMP speech_command ($F42E). Called by the game's speech routine $8DB9 (A = phrase 1-4, then A = $FF in a loop until the phrase has ended, so the game waits for it). A = 0-$FC: play that phrase; $FF: return the status (bit 0 set while playing); $FE: stop; $FD: set the data base address from X/Y. The player (speech data included, $F000-$FF9B) runs from the NMI of CIA 2 timer B and writes 4-bit samples to the SID volume register $D418; research.md credits the game's speech to Electronic Speech Systems.

Speech NMI, first part of a pitch period: writes the next buffer byte / 2 to $D418 (LDA $F000 with its low byte at $F085 self-modified, stepped forward), acknowledges CIA 2 ($DD0D read by CMP), counts $FD down; at 0 switches the NMI vector to nmi_play_backward and starts it from the same position ($F0A6 = $F085).
Low byte of the LDA $F000 at $F084: the buffer position being played forward, set from speech_play_start at each period ($F0FB) and incremented per sample ($F092).
End of the forward half: NMI vector low byte = $A4 (nmi_play_backward), backward position = the forward one.

Speech NMI, second part of a pitch period: plays the same samples in reverse order (LDA $F000 with the low byte at $F0A6 decremented), counting $FE down; at the end goes to the silence (nmi_silence_start, vector $C3) when the period has a gap ($FF non-zero), else straight to nmi_period_end. Playing each chunk forward and then backward makes a symmetric pulse from half the data.
Low byte of the LDA $F000 at $F0A5: the buffer position being played backward (set at $F09F, decremented at $F0B3).
End of the backward half: with a gap ($FF non-zero) the next NMI is nmi_silence_start, otherwise the period ends at once.

Speech NMI: the silent gap that completes a voiced pitch period (its length $FF, from speech_gap_length, sets the pitch), and the whole period of a pause frame. Writes the mid level 7 to $D418 once (LDA #$0E / LSR), then leaves the counting to nmi_silence ($F0D9); at the end, nmi_period_end. Also the first NMI after speech_command starts a phrase.
Speech NMI during a gap: acknowledges CIA 2 and counts $FF down, writing nothing; at 0 goes on to nmi_period_end ($F0F1).

Speech NMI after the last frame (vector set through speech_period_handler = $E1 by $F17E): stops CIA 2 timer B ($DD0F = $90, so no further NMI) and leaves $D418 at 7. From then on speech_status reports bit 0 clear.

Start of the next pitch period (entered from the NMI handlers): NMI vector low byte from speech_period_handler, forward index from speech_play_start, $FD = $FE = speech_half_length, $FF = speech_gap_length; counts speech_periods_left up and, while it has not wrapped, jumps through the self-modified JMP at $F110 to the per-period work of the frame type (rti only, $F13C voiced, $F154 unvoiced); when it wraps, saves X and Y and calls speech_next_chunk.
Low byte of the JMP $F13A at $F110, set per frame type: $3A = nothing (pause frames, $F253), $3C = speech_voiced_period ($F23C), $54 = speech_unvoiced_period ($F216).
Periods for this chunk used up: call speech_next_chunk with X and Y saved, then return from the NMI.

Called from the NMI when a chunk's periods are used up: counts speech_chunks_left up and at 0 reads the next frame record (speech_read_frame). Entry $F125 (speech_start_chunk) goes on: speech_periods_left = speech_periods_reload, X = the buffer half not playing, then JMP through the self-modified JMP at $F137 to the decoder of the frame's type, which fills that half.
Entry used by speech_command ($F459) to set up the first chunk of a phrase: reads the first frame record ($F1BC) and decodes it; see speech_next_chunk.

Low byte of the JMP at $F137, set per frame: $8F type 1 (1-bit samples, $F18F), $9B type 2 (4-bit samples, $F19B), $92 type 0 and $95 type 3 (2-bit samples, $F192/$F195), $84 a pause frame ($F184), $7E after the last frame ($F17E, stop).
Per-period work for pause frames: none (PLA, RTI).

Per-period work for voiced frames (types 2 and 3), from the NMI: unless the played waveform is already the new chunk, blends it halfway toward it again (speech_crossfade), then steps the pitch (speech_pitch_step). X and Y saved.
Voiced period: pitch step, restore X and Y, return from the NMI.

Per-period work for unvoiced frames (types 0 and 1), from the NMI: slides the played window along the chunk, start + speech_window_step and length - speech_window_step, until the length is $10, then starts again from the whole chunk (length speech_chunk_length). There is no gap between periods ($FF = 0), so this is noise-like sound with no pitch.
Unvoiced window at its minimum: back to the start of the chunk's half with the full length.
Decoder slot used after the last frame: speech_period_handler = $E1, so the next period is nmi_speech_stop.
Decoder slot for a pause frame: speech_period_handler = $C3 (the silence handler) and a gap of $80 samples, so each period is 128 samples of level 7.
Decoder slot for type 1 frames: JMP speech_decode_1bit ($F372).
Decoder slot for type 0 frames: JMP speech_decode_2bit_fixed ($F3E2). No frame of the five phrases has type 0 (simulator, all five played).

Decoder slot for type 3 frames: 2-bit samples with a chosen scale (speech_decode_2bit, $F267), then the same switch or blend as type 2. No frame of the five phrases has type 3 (simulator, all five played).
Decoder slot for type 2 frames: 4-bit samples (speech_decode_4bit, $F2E4) into the idle half.

After a voiced chunk is decoded: if bit 4 of the frame's first byte ($F1BD) is still set, clears it and switches playback straight to the new chunk (speech_play_start = speech_new_half), so only a frame's first chunk can cut in; otherwise blends toward it (speech_crossfade). Then steps the pitch.
Voiced chunk without a hard switch: blend, then pitch step.

Reads the next 4-byte frame record through ($F5) unless the previous frame's first byte (kept as the operand at $F1BD) had bit 5 set, which marks the last frame: then the decoder slot becomes speech_set_stop. Byte 0: bit 7-6 the voiced chunk length (8, 16, 24 or 32 samples via $F24D), bit 6 also the unvoiced length ($40 or $20), bit 5 last frame, bit 4 hard switch, bits 3-0 give 16 - n periods per chunk (speech_periods_reload). Byte 1: bits 7-3 give 32 - n chunks in the frame (speech_chunks_left), bit 2 a pause frame (no samples), bits 1-0 the type (0, 1 unvoiced; 2, 3 voiced). Bytes 2-3: the samples, as an offset from speech_data_base. Sets the per-period job and the decoder slot, then advances ($F5) by 4 (speech_next_frame).

Operand of the LDA #$00 at $F1BC: the current frame's first byte (written at $F1CC), so that the next call can test its last-frame bit; bit 4 is cleared by speech_switch_or_blend after use; zeroed by speech_find_phrase ($F4D4).
Half-waveform lengths of voiced frames, by bits 7-6 of the frame's first byte: 8, 16, 24, 32 samples ($F234).
A frame with bit 2 of byte 1 set: no samples; per-period job none ($3A), decoder slot speech_set_pause ($84).
Advances the frame pointer $F5/$F6 by 4, to the next record.

2-bit decoder with a chosen scale (type 3, unused by the five phrases): writes speech_half_length samples into the idle half starting at X; the chunk's first byte picks one of the level tables at $F2D4 + 4 x (bits 1-0) (1: $0C-$12, 2: $08-$14, 3: $02-$1A; 0 would take code bytes at $F2D4) and supplies three samples, then four samples per byte, low bits first. Keeps the half in speech_new_half. The stop value is written into the CPX at $F2D3.
Entry shared with speech_decode_2bit_fixed: A = the first byte, the level table picked from its low 2 bits.
Operand of the LDA #$00 at $F2A1: the data byte being unpacked by the 2-bit decoder (written at $F274 and $F295).
Operand of the CPX #$00 at $F2D3: where the 2-bit decoders stop (X start + length, written at $F26A and $F3E8). The bytes from $F2D4 are also level table 0 in speech_decode_2bit.

The 2-bit decoders' level tables, 4 entries each (doubled volumes): scale 1 $0C $0E $10 $12 (volume 6-9), scale 2 $08 $0C $10 $14 (4-10), scale 3 $02 $0A $12 $1A (1-13). Used by types 0 and 3 only, which no phrase in this image uses.

4-bit decoder (type 2, the voiced frames): writes speech_half_length samples into the idle half starting at X, two per data byte: high nibble, then low nibble, each doubled (AND $1E) so that the LSR at play time gives volume 0-15. Keeps the half in speech_new_half; the stop value goes into the CPX at $F317.
Operand of the CPX #$00 at $F317: where speech_decode_4bit stops (written at $F2E7).

Once per voiced period: counts the pitch record's periods ($F4E4) up; while running, adds the slope speech_pitch_slope to the pitch speech_pitch and sets the gap speech_gap_length = pitch / 2; when it wraps, reads the next 2-byte pitch record through ($F7): byte 0 AND $FE the new pitch; byte 1 high nibble 16 - n periods, low nibble the slope's index into speech_slopes ($F362).
Next pitch record: pitch, count, slope, then advance ($F7) by 2 and set the gap.
Pitch slopes by the low nibble of a pitch record's second byte: -12, -10, -8, -6, -4, -2, -1, 0, +1, +2, +4, +6, +8, +10, +12, +14 added to the doubled pitch each period, so the pitch glides.

1-bit decoder (type 1, the unvoiced frames): sets speech_play_start = the idle half and speech_half_length = speech_chunk_length, then writes one sample per bit, $0E or $10 (volume 7 or 8), low bit first, 8 per data byte (the first byte gives fewer), until the stop value at $F3AA. A two-level noise: enough for hiss sounds like S and SH.
Operand of the CPX #$00 at $F3A9: where speech_decode_1bit stops (written at $F378).
Writes four one-bit samples from A (low bit first; the rest kept in Y) into the buffer at X. Entry $F3C3 writes the current sample and then three more from Y.
Second entry of speech_unpack_bits: stores A, then three more bits from Y.

2-bit decoder with the fixed scale 1 (type 0, unused by the five phrases): sets speech_play_start and speech_half_length = speech_chunk_length like the 1-bit decoder, forces the level-table bits of the first byte to 1, and joins speech_decode_2bit at $F274.

Blends the waveform being played (at speech_play_start) with the newly decoded chunk (at speech_new_half), sample by sample, (a + b + 1) / 2, into the quarter $20 or $60 of the buffer not in use, over speech_half_length samples, and makes that the one played. Called once per voiced period, it moves the sound halfway to the new chunk each time: a smooth change of waveform. The self-modified operands $F417, $F41B and $F41F are the three low bytes.
Low byte of the LDA $F000,X at $F416: the new chunk (speech_new_half, $F407).
Low byte of the ADC $F000,X at $F41A: the waveform being played (speech_play_start, $F401).
Low byte of the STA $F000,X at $F41E: the blend's destination, $20 or $60 ($F413), which becomes speech_play_start ($F42A).

The command dispatcher behind speech_call: $FF returns the status; $FE stops the timer ($F46D); $FD stores X/Y as the data base ($F475); any other A is a phrase number: finds it (speech_find_phrase), stops any speech, and unless the KERNAL ROM is switched in (status negative) starts it: speech_play_start = 0, $FC = $F2 (the level tables' page), NMI vector $FFFA/$FFFB = $F0C3, a one-sample gap ($FF = 1), the first chunk decoded (speech_start_chunk), CIA 2 timer B started (speech_timer_start). Returns the status. A phrase number above 4 reads past the table (the game passes 1-4 only).

Status for the caller: A = $80 (negative) when bit 1 of $01 (HIRAM) is set, that is with the KERNAL ROM in and the NMI vector not the player's; otherwise bit 0 of $DD0F, 1 while CIA 2 timer B runs (a phrase is playing).
Stops CIA 2 timer B ($DD0F = $90), ending the NMIs, and returns the status.
Command $FD: X/Y (low/high) become speech_data_base. The game never sends it; the base in the image, $F4EA, is used.

Starts CIA 2 timer B for the speech NMI: $DD0F = $91 (start, force load, continuous), latch $0065, so an NMI every 102 cycles, 9,659 Hz on PAL (985,248 / 102) and 10,027 Hz on NTSC, which plays speech about 4 % higher and faster; enables its interrupt ($DD0D = $82) and clears pending flags.

Looks phrase A up in the table at speech_data_base (4 bytes per phrase, pointer ($F9)): the first word + base is the pitch list, into $F7/$F8; the second word + base the frame list, into $F5/$F6; pitch counter $F4E4 = $FF so the first period reads a pitch record; speech_frame_flags = 0.
Two bytes ($00, $FF) between the player's code and its variables that no instruction names and no phrase reads: unused.

Low byte of the NMI handler each pitch period starts with (copied into $FFFA at $F0F2): $83 play the waveform (nmi_play_forward, set at $F1F1), $C3 silence (a pause frame, $F186), $E1 stop (after the last frame, $F180).

Where in speech_wave_buffer the waveform being played starts (low byte): its bit 6 picks the half, so the decoders fill the other one. Set to 0 by speech_command ($F444), by the decoders ($F372, $F3E2), by the hard switch ($F1B0), by speech_crossfade ($F42A) and moved by the unvoiced window ($F169).
Samples in the waveform's half, played forward then backward each period ($FD/$FE reload at $F0FE): 8-32 for voiced frames ($F237), the window length for unvoiced ones ($F15F, $F179, $F37E, $F3EE).

Samples of silence ending each period ($FF reload at $F105): pitch / 2 for voiced frames (speech_pitch_step $F32C/$F35E), 0 for unvoiced ones ($F219), $80 for pauses ($F18B). The longer the gap, the lower the voice.
Chunks left in the current frame, counted up to 0 (32 - n from the frame record's second byte, $F1DC; incremented at $F120).
Periods each chunk is played, as a count up to 0: $F0 OR the low nibble of the frame's first byte ($F1D1), copied into speech_periods_left at each chunk ($F12B).
Periods left of the current chunk, counted up once per period by nmi_period_end ($F10B); at 0 the next chunk is decoded.
Unvoiced frames: the chunk's length in samples, $40 or $20 by bit 6 of the frame's first byte ($F20B), and the full window length ($F176).
Unvoiced frames: how far the window slides each period, speech_chunk_length / 8 ($F211; read at $F15C, $F166).
Start (low byte) of the half holding the chunk just decoded ($F26D, $F2EA); speech_voiced_period compares it with speech_play_start to see whether a blend is still needed.
Periods left for the current pitch record, counted up to 0 ($F31C): 16 - the high nibble of its second byte ($F346); $FF after speech_find_phrase so the first period reads a record.
The doubled pitch value: the gap is half of it. From a pitch record's first byte ($F337), plus speech_pitch_slope each period ($F328).
Signed change of speech_pitch per period, from speech_slopes by the record's low nibble ($F351).

Base address of the speech data, low byte here and high byte at $F4E8: $F4EA in the image, where speech_phrase_table is. Every pointer in the data is an offset from it (added at $F1E4, $F49E, $F4AF, $F4C5). Changeable by command $FD, which the game never sends.
High byte of speech_data_base ($F4).
One byte ($FF) before the phrase table, named by no instruction: unused.

Five phrases, 4 bytes each: the pitch list's offset and the frame list's offset from speech_data_base ($F4EA). Phrase 0: pitch $F4FE, frames $F688; 1: $F524, $F6BC; 2: $F558, $F6F0; 3: $F580, $F70C; 4: $F5D6, $F75C. The game asks for 1-4 only (phrase 1 from $62ED, $6393 and $8820; 2 from $874B; 3 from $62F2, $8AB9 and $8D1F; 4 from $8C5A), so phrase 0 is never heard. Lengths in the simulator (PAL): 0.95, 1.61, 1.33, 2.69 and 2.23 seconds.

Pitch lists, 2-byte records read by speech_pitch_step: byte 0 AND $FE the doubled pitch (gap = half of it, in samples), byte 1 high nibble 16 - n voiced periods, low nibble the slope (speech_slopes). Phrase 0's list, $F4FE-$F523 (19 records in the simulator).
Pitch list of phrase 1, $F524-$F557 (26 records read in the simulator).
Pitch list of phrase 2, $F558-$F57F; its last record read, at $F580, is also phrase 3's first.
Pitch list of phrase 3, $F580-$F5D5 (44 records read, the last at $F5D6 being phrase 4's first).
Pitch list of phrase 4, $F5D6-$F687, the longest (90 records read in the simulator; the last read, at $F688, is really the first frame record: the phrase ends before it matters).

Frame lists, 4-byte records read by speech_read_frame (flags and chunk length; periods and chunks, pause, type; sample offset from $F4EA). Phrase 0: 13 frames, $F688-$F6BB; it starts with the same sample blocks as phrase 1 ($F768, $F800, $F778...), a shorter version of it.
Frame list of phrase 1: 13 frames, $F6BC-$F6EF. Phrase 1 is the one the title plays on SPACE, the "Ghostbusters!" the manual describes.
Frame list of phrase 2: 7 frames, $F6F0-$F70B.
Frame list of phrase 3: 20 frames, $F70C-$F75B; the same two sample blocks ($FBC0, $FC70) alternate four times in it, a repeated syllable.
Frame list of phrase 4: 3 long voiced frames, $F75C-$F767.

Sample data, $F768-$FF9B: 1-bit chunks for unvoiced frames, 4-bit (two samples a byte) for voiced ones, addressed by the frame records. Phrases 0 and 1 share $F768-$F8C7; phrase 0 also reads $F8C0-$F967.
Eight bytes ($F968-$F96F) between phrase 0's samples and phrase 1's second block that no phrase reads (simulator, all five phrases played).
Samples of phrase 1's last voiced frame, $F970-$FA2F.
Samples of phrase 2, $FA30-$FBBF.
Samples of phrase 3, $FBC0-$FDB3.
Inside phrase 3's samples. The label is only there because the dead tape loader calls the KERNAL at $FC93 ($CE7D); with the ROM switched in that call goes to the KERNAL, not to these bytes.
Inside phrase 3's samples; labelled only because tape_load_fail jumps to the KERNAL's reset at $FCE2 ($CED3), which is ROM, not these bytes.
Inside phrase 3's samples; labelled only because the dead tape loader calls the KERNAL at $FD15 ($CE83), which is ROM, not these bytes.
Last part of phrase 3's samples ($FDA3-$FDB3); labelled only because the dead tape loader calls the KERNAL's IOINIT at $FDA3 ($CE80), which is ROM, not these bytes.
Samples of phrase 4, $FDB4-$FF9B: three voiced frames of 4-bit data.

94 bytes after the speech data: $FF x 17, then bytes that look like multicolour graphics ($55, $AA, $FC patterns, $01 $04 $10 $40...). No instruction names $FF9C-$FFF9, no simulator run reads it, and play-map.vsf holds the same bytes as entry.vsf: unused, a left-over.

The hardware NMI vector (RAM, the KERNAL being banked out): $6425 (nmi_restore_handler) from cold_start ($600E/$6013) and again after speech ($8E31/$8E36); $F0C3 while the speech player runs ($F44B/$F452), whose handlers change the low byte every few samples ($F099, $F0BE, $F0D4, $F0F5). The image's $A4A3 here is never used: cold_start writes the vector before any NMI can occur.
The RESET vector's RAM copy: a reset always reads the KERNAL ROM (which the reset itself switches in), so these bytes ($A6A5 in the image) are never used; no instruction names them.
The hardware IRQ vector: $8E76 (the raster IRQ) from cold_start ($6018/$601D), before interrupts are enabled; the image's $92A7 is never used. Written only there.
